gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i2: Skipping zero characters returns 0 and does not move the position.
ADDED i3: When the emulated size is negative the reader is already at/past the end, so skip() reports end-of-file by returning the (negative) size.
ADDED i4: Reading past the marked read limit makes the mark invalid, so reset() fails with an IOException.
ADDED i6: reset() on a reader created with mark support disabled is unsupported.
ADDED i8: Calling reset() on the shared INSTANCE before any position is marked throws an IOException.
ADDED i10: Reading into an array advances the position by the array length.
ADDED i11: Skipping past the end of a size 0 reader marks it as end-of-file, so the next read() reports reading after end of file.
ADDED i13: Reading into an empty array returns 0 without touching the position.
ADDED i14: A size 0 reader reaches end-of-file on the first read(); a second read() then throws because it is reading after end of file.
ADDED i16: mark() on a reader created with mark support disabled is unsupported.
ADDED i18: A reader configured to throw on EOF raises an EOFException when skip() is called after the position has reached the (negative) size.
ADDED i20: close() resets internal state while size and mark support are unchanged.
ADDED i21: Skipping past the end of a size 0 reader leaves it at end-of-file, so a subsequent skip() reports skipping after end of file.
ADDED i23: getSize() can be queried right after construction; mark is supported by default.
ADDED i24: The default constructors enable mark support.
ADDED i25: A freshly constructed reader starts at position 0 and keeps its size.
ADDED i26: Reading a single character returns 0 (the default char) and advances the position.
